original: That second theorem isn't a gap in the VM. Pricing every merge would charge every overwrite: every \texttt{LOAD\_IMM}, every \texttt{ADD}, every \texttt{STORE}. That is what Landauer's principle asks of a physical machine, and whether every account of computation has to answer to it is the physics question this book leaves open. The VM's schedule keeps classical computation free and puts the price on certification alone. A2 holds for it as a theorem either way. What the finite argument adds is that the price isn't arbitrary: on hardware that does price its merges, the same bill comes due. So I built a finite machine that prices all its merges and showed the VM runs it.
